NONE: C1 to make a choice, especially of one thing or possibility instead of others
選擇，挑選；（尤指）優先選擇

example: Mike opted for early retirement.
麥克選擇了提前退休。
[ + to infinitive ] Most people opt to have the operation.
大多數人選擇動手術。

NONE: › to choose to be part of an activity, arrangement, etc.
主動選擇加入
› the fact of choosing to take part in an activity, arrangement, etc. rather than being forced to take part
主動選擇加入

example: Company policy is to leave new workers out of the pension scheme, unless they choose to opt in.
公司政策是新員工除非主動要求加入，否則不把他們列入養老金計畫內。
It is an opt-in rather than an opt-out system, which means that permission must be sought on a case-by-case basis.
這是一個主動選擇加入而非主動選擇退出的系統，這就意味著准許令必須酌情逐個考慮。

NONE: › to choose not to be part of an activity or to stop being involved in it
選擇不參與；選擇退出
› a situation in which some members of a group choose not to join or be involved in an activity
主動選擇退出

example: Within any society, there will usually be people who decide to opt out (= choose not to live the way most people do).
通常，任何社會都會有人決定不按常規方式生活。
Employees can choose to opt out of the pension scheme.
個人可以選擇不參加養老金制度。
Since the opt-out, the hospital has been responsible for its own budgeting.
自從主動選擇退出後，這家醫院要對自己的預算負責。

NONE: › relating to light or the eyes
光學的；眼睛的；視覺的

example: a fibre optic cable
纖維光纜

NONE: › the group of nerve fibres (= structures like threads) that pass signals from the retina at the back of each eye to the brain
視神經（形如細絲的神經纖維束，將視覺訊號從眼球後部的視網膜傳送至大腦）
› relating to light or the ability to see
光學的；視覺的；視力的

example: an optical effect
視覺效果
an optical microscope
光學顯微鏡

NONE: › the process by which an electronic device recognizes printed or written letters or numbers
光符識別，光學文字辨識（用電子儀器識別印刷或書寫字元的過程）
› a long, thin glass rod through which very large amounts of information can be sent in the form of light
光學纖維，光纖

example: See also
fibre optics

NONE: › something that tricks your eyes and makes you think you see something that is not really there, or see it differently from how it really is
視錯覺；光幻覺
› UK also ophthalmic optician, US optometrist someone whose job is examining people's eyes and selling glasses or contact lenses to correct sight problems
視光師；配鏡師
› US UK dispensing optician a person whose job is fitting and selling glasses and contact lenses to correct sight problems, but who does not examine people's eyes
眼鏡銷售員

example: Compare
ophthalmologist

U: › the study of light and of instruments using light

NONE: optimum
C2 the quality of being full of hope and emphasizing the good parts of a situation, or a belief that something good will happen
樂觀；樂觀主義

example: There was a note of optimism in his voice as he spoke about the company's future.
談到公司的未來，他語氣裡帶著樂觀情緒。
They had cause/grounds/reason for cautious optimism about an improvement in her medical condition.
他們對她的病情持謹慎的樂觀態度。
Opposite
pessimism

NONE: C1 someone who always believes that good things will happen
樂觀主義者，樂天派

example: She's a born optimist (= someone who has always been optimistic).
她天生是個樂天派。

NONE: B2 hoping or believing that good things will happen in the future
樂觀的

example: She is optimistic about her chances of winning a gold medal.
她對贏得金牌很樂觀。

NONE: › the act of making something as good as possible
優化，完善

example: the optimization of chemical processes
對化學工序流程的優化

NONE: › to make something as good as possible
使優化，完善

example: We need to optimize our use of the existing technology.
我們需要充分利用現有技術。

NONE: › best; most likely to bring success or advantage
最優的，最佳的；優化的

example: A mixture of selected funds is an optimum choice for future security and return on investment.
同時選擇幾種基金是確保未來投資安全和投資收益的最佳選擇。

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] one thing that can be chosen from a set of possibilities, or the freedom to make a choice
C: › [ C ] specialized finance & economics the right to buy something in the future
C1 to have to do a particular thing because there is no possibility of doing anything else

example: The best option would be to cancel the trip altogether.
最好的選擇是徹底取消這次行程。
There are various options open to someone who is willing to work hard.
願意努力工作的人有多種選項。
They didn't leave him much option - either he paid or they'd beat him up.
他們沒有給他多少選擇餘地——要不付錢，要不挨打。
UK a share option
股票期權
US a stock option
股票期權
The publishers decided not to take up their option on the paperback version.
出版商決定放棄平裝版的購買權。
After her appalling behaviour, we had no option but to dismiss her.
鑒於她的惡劣行為，我們別無選擇，只能解僱她。

NONE: B2 If something is optional, you can choose if you want to do it, pay it, buy it, etc.
可選擇的；非強制的

example: English is compulsory for all students, but art and music are optional.
英語是所有學生的必修課，而藝術和音樂則是選修的。
